name: Vigilius Tapsensis
pdTranslations: None identified in CCEL, NPNF, or ANF collections.
modernTranslations: No comprehensive English translation located. Works remain primarily in Latin manuscripts.
untranslatedHighlights: Contra Eutychetem (five books); Contra Arianos, Sabellianos, et Photinianos; various polemical treatises against Eutychianism and Arianism.

name: Anselmus Laudunensis
pdTranslations: Some biblical commentaries available in older theological indexes; not systematically translated.
modernTranslations: Fragmentary translations of Glosae on Matthew and John exist in scholarly editions; not comprehensive modern English translation.
untranslatedHighlights: Glosae super Iohannem and most biblical commentaries remain in Latin; systematically unpublished in English.

name: Lanfrancus Cantuariensis
pdTranslations: None in ANF/NPNF; limited scholarly facing-page translations of selected letters.
modernTranslations: Letters of Lanfranc have been edited with facing-page English translation by scholarly editions; theological treatises remain largely in Latin.
untranslatedHighlights: Consuetudines; most theological writings on Eucharist and reform remain in Latin.

name: Ratherius Veronensis
modernTranslations: Corpus Christianorum edition (CC 46, 46A) provides critical Latin text; no comprehensive English translation identified.
untranslatedHighlights: Praeloquia (Prefaces in six books); numerous epistles and treatises on clerical reform remain untranslated.

name: Herbertus de Boseham
modernTranslations: Medieval biblical commentaries remain in Latin; known for Hebrew Psalter commentary but no modern English translation published.
untranslatedHighlights: Commentary on Jerome's Hebrew Psalter; revision of Peter Lombard's Great Gloss on Psalms and Epistles; all major works remain in Latin.

name: Gregorius VII
pdTranslations: None (modern work, all translations are scholarly editions).
modernTranslations: The Register of Pope Gregory VII (1073-1085): complete English translation by H. E. J. Cowdrey (Oxford University Press); selected letters also translated in various scholarly editions and databases.
untranslatedHighlights: None; primary corpus fully translated.

name: Nicolaus I
modernTranslations: Responses of Pope Nicholas I to the Questions of the Bulgars (A.D. 866) translated by W. L. North; individual letters translated in Epistolae database; broader Register not fully translated.
untranslatedHighlights: Complete Register remains partially untranslated; some surviving letters have selective translation coverage only.

name: Othlonus S. Emmerammi Ratisponensis
modernTranslations: No comprehensive English translation. Works preserved in Patrologia Latina Vol. 146; scholarly editions exist in German but not English.
untranslatedHighlights: All major works—theological treatises, spiritual writings, annales—remain in Latin only.

name: Cyprianus Carthaginensis
pdTranslations: ANF Vol. 5 (Ante-Nicene Fathers), translated by Robert Ernest Wallis (1886); includes epistles, treatises on Unity of Church, Mortality, Lapsed, Novatian controversy.
modernTranslations: NPNF ANF Vol. 5 (Schaff edition); widely available in CCEL; comprehensive modern English coverage of all major works.
untranslatedHighlights: None; corpus essentially complete in English.

name: Balduinus Cantuariensis
modernTranslations: Isolated medieval works translated; De commendatione fidei known from monastic florilegia; facing-page translations exist in academic editions but no comprehensive modern English version.
untranslatedHighlights: Sermones remain largely untranslated; theological treatises on faith and monastic practice in Latin.

name: Petrus Chrysologus
modernTranslations: Fathers of the Church Series: FOTC Vol. 17 (G. Ganss, 1953); FOTC Vol. 109 (W. B. Palardy, 2004); FOTC Vol. 110 (W. B. Palardy, 2005). All authentic sermons now fully translated. Recent Routledge edition (D. V. Meconi Jr., 2020).
untranslatedHighlights: None; all genuine sermons covered in modern English.

name: Alulfus Tornacensis
modernTranslations: No comprehensive English translation. Medieval Benedictine monk's commentaries on Scripture (Opus exceptionum Gregorianum) remain in Latin; critical editions exist but no English version.
untranslatedHighlights: De Expositione Novi Testamenti; biblical commentaries compiled from Gregory; Gregorialis (anthology from Gregory's Moralia)—all in Latin.

name: Paulinus Nolanus
pdTranslations: None in ANF/NPNF (author lived after collections' main scope).
modernTranslations: Ancient Christian Writers (ACW) series: ACW 035-036 (Letters, 1-22 and 23-51, P.G. Walsh, 1966-1967); ACW 040 (Poems/Carmina, P.G. Walsh, 1975). Comprehensive English translation by major patristic series.
untranslatedHighlights: None; letters and poems fully covered in ACW.

name: Landulfus Sagax
modernTranslations: Historia Romana (Historia Miscella) remains in Latin; no comprehensive English translation located.
untranslatedHighlights: Historia Romana/Historia Miscella—primary work remains untranslated.

name: Florus Lugdunensis
modernTranslations: Sermon on Predestination translated in Gottschalk & A Medieval Predestination Controversy: Texts Translated from the Latin (Marquette University Press, 2010); major work (Exposition on Pauline Epistles) remains in Latin.
untranslatedHighlights: Expositio on letters of Saint Paul from Augustine (monumental work); most other theological and canonical writings remain in Latin.

name: Hugo Flaviniacensis
modernTranslations: Chronicle (Chronicon Virdunense seu Flaviniacense) remains primarily in Latin; no comprehensive modern English translation found.
untranslatedHighlights: Chronicle (two books, extending 1002-1112); all major historical and ecclesiastical writings remain in Latin.

name: Rodulfus Trudonis
modernTranslations: Gesta abbatum Trudonensium (seven books) remains in Latin; no comprehensive English translation located.
untranslatedHighlights: Gesta abbatum Trudonensium (historiographical account of abbots of St. Trond in seven books)—entirely in Latin.

name: Robertus Pullus
modernTranslations: Sententiarum Theologicarum Libri Octo remains in Latin; no modern comprehensive English translation.
untranslatedHighlights: Sententiarum Theologicarum Libri Octo (theological compendium, served as official university textbook); all major works remain untranslated.

name: Justinianus I Augustus
modernTranslations: Corpus Juris Civilis: Institutes translated (first part translated 1756 by George Harris; multiple modern editions); Novels (Novellae Constitutiones) fully translated with annotations by David J.D. Miller and Peter Sarris (modern edition). Digest and Code have limited English translation.
untranslatedHighlights: Digest remains substantially untranslated; Code only partially translated; focus has been Institutes and Novels.

name: Origenes
pdTranslations: ANF Vol. 4 (Contra Celsus, de Principiis); ANF Vol. 9 (Commentary on Matthew, Commentary on John); Ante-Nicene Fathers translation via Rufinus' Latin versions.
modernTranslations: NPNF ANF volumes provide Rufinus' Latin translations in English. Some fragmentary modern translations exist; works remain dependent on Rufinus' medieval translation layer rather than direct Greek/Latin access.
untranslatedHighlights: Homilies on Genesis and other biblical books translated by Rufinus but not systematically in modern English; many Greek fragments remain untranslated.
